research_rationale: EO 12332 (Nov. 10, 1981; 46 FR 55913) established the National Productivity Advisory Committee under FACA. All twelve operative subsections (secs. 1(a)-4(b)) concern that Committee: composition, advisory functions, agency information, unpaid service, Treasury support, the Executive Secretary, the FACA delegation to the Secretary of the Treasury, and the sec. 4(b) sunset of December 31, 1982 'unless sooner extended'. EO 12399 sec. 1(l), effective December 31, 1982 (sec. 6), continued the Committee 'until September 30, 1984'. The next continuance order, EO 12489 (Sept. 28, 1984), lists other committees but not this one, and no other held order, OFR catalog note or the 1989 Codification ('Continued by EO 12399'; 'Revoked by EO 12534') shows a further extension. The Committee therefore terminated on September 30, 1984, which is the first end of every clause and the whole-order end. EO 12534 sec. 3(f), effective September 30, 1985 (sec. 5), revoked the order as one 'which established committees that have terminated'; it is a later event, not the first end. The draft's FULL_AND_PARTIAL_EVIDENCE_CONFLICT is resolved by reading EO 12534 sec. 3, which revokes each listed order as a whole; the 'partial' reading came only from the OFR catalog's acting-order phrasing 'Revokes advisory committees established by'. Quotations are verbatim from the saved govinfo OCR text of the Federal Register issue, which is letter-spaced on these pages; the pdfplumber recheck text has the same wording. The draft's page range (PDF pages 11-17) ran into later documents and is corrected to pages 11-12. No human certification is asserted.

research_rationale: EO 12369 (June 30, 1982; 47 FR 28899) established the Executive Committee of the President's Private Sector Survey on Cost Control under FACA. Its twelve operative subsections (secs. 1(a)-4(b), with the five recommendation areas inside sec. 2(c)) all concern that Committee. Section 4(b) set termination on December 31, 1982 'unless sooner extended'. Each term was extended before it lapsed: EO 12398 (Dec. 31, 1982; also raised membership to 170) to June 30, 1983; EO 12429 (June 28, 1983) to October 30, 1983; EO 12447 (Oct. 27, 1983) to December 31, 1983; EO 12455 (Dec. 29, 1983) to January 31, 1984. None of these states a separate effective date, so each took effect on signing. No later extension appears in the held order texts, the OFR catalog notes or the 1989 Codification (amendments listed are exactly these four), and the Committee is not in the continuance orders EO 12399 or EO 12489. The Committee and every clause therefore ended on January 31, 1984 (whole-order end). EO 12534 sec. 3(b), effective September 30, 1985, is a later cleanup revocation. The draft's FULL_AND_PARTIAL_EVIDENCE_CONFLICT is resolved by reading EO 12534 sec. 3, which revokes each listed order as a whole; the 'partial' reading came only from the OFR catalog's acting-order phrasing 'Revokes advisory committees established by'. research_rationale: EO 12400 (Jan. 3, 1983; 48 FR 381) established the President's Commission on Strategic Forces under FACA; its nine operative subsections all concern that Commission. Original sec. 4(b) ended it 30 days after its report (due February 18, 1983). EO 12406 (Feb. 18, 1983) moved the report deadline to April 15, 1983 and the end to 60 days after reporting; EO 12424 (June 10, 1983), which records the report as 'dated April 11, 1983', gave the Commission a new review mandate (sec. 2(a)), a report deadline of December 15, 1983 (sec. 2(b)) and a fixed end: 'terminate on January 3, 1984, unless sooner extended' (sec. 4(b)). EO 12424 was signed on the 60th day after April 11, 1983, so the Commission did not lapse before the extension (if the report reached the President later than its date, the margin is larger). No later extension appears in the held order texts, the OFR catalog notes or the 1989 Codification (amendments listed: EOs 12406, 12424), and the Commission is not in continuance order EO 12489. The Commission and every clause therefore ended on January 3, 1984 (whole-order end). EO 12534 sec. 3(k), effective September 30, 1985, is a later cleanup revocation. The draft's FULL_AND_PARTIAL_EVIDENCE_CONFLICT is resolved by reading EO 12534 sec. 3, which revokes each listed order as a whole; the 'partial' reading came only from the OFR catalog's acting-order phrasing 'Revokes advisory committees established by'. No human certification is asserted.

No rights, entitlements, property, delegations or functions outside the body itself were created, so nothing survives its termination; reimbursements and support given while it existed are completed transactions, not continuing effects. Bounded search: the full original order, every amending and continuance order named in this claim, and EO 12534.

research_rationale: EO 9451 (June 20, 1944; 9 FR 6905) has one operative provision: paragraph 2 of EO 9243 (priority classifications among departments and agencies for the transfer and release of Federal personnel) 'is hereby revoked, effective as of July 1, 1944.' Its only effect is that partial revocation of EO 9243. EO 9695 para. 1 (Feb. 8, 1946; 11 FR 1559) revoked EO 9243 as a whole; it states no effective date, so it took effect on signing. Following the 1989 Codification's treatment of this order ('Amended EO 9243'; 'Revoked by EO 9695'), the amendment's lifecycle ends with the revocation of the order it amended, on February 8, 1946; the revocation of para. 2 itself had already taken effect on July 1, 1944 and was never reversed (EO 9695 revives nothing). No other order touched EO 9243 para. 2 in between (OFR catalog and saved later texts show no citation of this order). A reviewer who instead treats a revoking provision as spent on its own effective date would date the end July 1, 1944; this claim adopts the Codification convention used for amending orders. No human certification is asserted.

Every clause is terminated (EO 12534 sec. 3 lists the order among those whose committees had terminated, and revoked it effective September 30, 1985), but the first-end date is left open rather than inferred from the deadline.
